title: Time, Speed and Distance
scientificNotes: General competitive-exam quantitative-aptitude topic; included to match the exam's Part A scope.
expression: Distance = Speed × Time    Relative speed (opposite directions) = S1 + S2    Relative speed (same direction) = |S1 − S2|
explanation: The core relationship Distance = Speed × Time underlies every variant. For two moving bodies, RELATIVE SPEED depends on direction: if moving TOWARD each other (opposite directions), relative speed is the SUM of their speeds (they close the gap faster together); if moving in the SAME direction, relative speed is the DIFFERENCE of their speeds (only the speed gap matters for one to catch up to/overtake the other). 'Trains crossing' problems additionally require adding the LENGTHS of the object(s) involved to the distance to be covered, since a train (or person) must cover its own length plus the other object's length to fully cross it. 'Boats and streams' problems use the same relative-speed logic: DOWNSTREAM speed = boat speed + stream speed (current helps); UPSTREAM speed = boat speed − stream speed (current hinders).

variables.meaning: Individual speeds of the two moving bodies
Distance to be covered (plus combined lengths, for crossing problems)

workedExample.scenario: A 120 m train crosses a 180 m platform completely at a speed of 20 m/s. Find the time taken.
workedExample.substitution: Total distance to cover = train length + platform length = 120 + 180 = 300 m. Time = Distance/Speed = 300/20

commonMistakes: Forgetting to add the OTHER object's length (platform, bridge, or second train) to the distance when a train 'crosses' something — only crossing a single stationary point (like a pole) uses just the train's own length.
Using the sum of speeds for two bodies moving in the SAME direction (should be the difference), or the difference for bodies moving in opposite directions (should be the sum).
genZNote: Trains crossing a platform aren't just covering their own length — they've got to clear the WHOLE platform too, nose to tail.
